title: Deepest Nested Substring
statement:
You are given a string `s` made of lowercase letters, digits and the three kinds of brackets `()`, `[]` and `{}`. The brackets are balanced: every opening bracket is closed by the matching closing bracket, and pairs are properly nested. Every bracket pair encloses at least one character (so `()` and `([])` never appear).

The **depth** of a bracket pair is `1` plus the number of bracket pairs that enclose it, so an outermost pair has depth `1`. Let `D` be the largest depth of any pair in `s`.

- If `s` contains no brackets (`D = 0`), the answer is the whole string `s`.
- Otherwise, the answer is the text strictly between the brackets of every pair of depth `D`. Such a pair contains no other bracket, so this text is made only of letters and digits. List the pieces in the order their opening brackets appear in `s`. If two different pairs enclose the same text, report it once for each pair.

Print every piece of the answer.
input_format: A single line containing the string `s` (no spaces).
output_format: Print the pieces of the answer, one per line, in the order described above.
constraints: s consists of lowercase letters, digits and the characters ( ) [ ] { }
the brackets are balanced and no bracket pair is empty

examples.explanation: The round pair has depth 1 and the square pair inside it has depth 2, which is the maximum. The text inside the square pair is `ghi`.
Both pairs are outermost, so both have the maximum depth 1. Their contents are reported left to right.
The maximum depth is 2. The pairs of depth 2 are `{b}`, `[e]` and `(g)`; the pairs `(...)` and `[...]` at the top have depth 1.

hints: The depth of a pair is the size of the stack of currently open brackets at the moment it closes.
Scan once with a stack of opening positions. When a closing bracket pops position `a` at index `i`, the depth of that pair is the stack size before the pop and its text is `s[a+1:i]`.
Keep the best depth seen so far and the list of texts at that depth; clear the list whenever you see a strictly deeper pair.
